## Review

**7 out of 10, Effective.** Presentation quality, judged with the SlideDeck Co review heuristic (https://slidedeck.co/review-methodology/). The ask, the evidence and the merit of the idea are not rated.

The deck has a clear spine: an eight-part outline on slide 3, divider slides, and a repeating pattern of an italic statement slide followed by a sourced chart with the finding in the title (slides 6-7, 8-9, 10-12). Charts are mostly legible with consistent colour, direct annotations and a source on every page. The weaknesses are consequential. Many statement slides are text-only and repeat what the next chart title says, and dense pages such as the generational tables (52-53), the McKinsey radar (15) and the Stitch Fix pages (69-70) use tiny type that is unreadable beyond a reader's desk. The long chain of macro slides (19-41) also delays the internet argument, and the 72 pages I could see are only about a third of 214.

**Worth keeping:** Keep the findings-as-titles, the consistent chart styling with direct callouts such as the 2008 and 2015 Asia-Pacific labels on slide 11, and the sourced footers.

**Most useful repair:** Fix the unreadable small type on slides 15, 52-53, 69 and 70 by cutting content or splitting the page, and make the dual-axis charts such as slide 12 easier to read by labelling the growth line directly.

**What would change the score:** Merge or cut the text-only statement slides that echo the following chart title, and compress the macro section so the internet-specific argument starts sooner.

_Confidence medium. 72 of 214 pages inspected on contact sheets, 4 at readable size. Reviewed Reviewed 2026-11-08. Model-assisted review (claude-sonnet-5-5)._

## Summary

This is Mary Meeker's Internet Trends 2016 deck, presented at the Code Conference on June 1, 2016, and published by KPCB. It opens with a title slide, a conference title slide, and an eight-part outline covering global internet users, macro trends, advertising and commerce, video, image and messaging, voice and transportation, China, public and private company data, and data privacy. It then moves through these sections in order, using large statistic-led headline slides followed by sourced bar and line charts, with the growth figure in each title and a footer carrying the source. Acknowledgements to partners, Hillhouse Capital and others appear early, before the data begins. The sections on advertising, commerce and messaging rely heavily on contrasting slides that pair a generation or platform with its behaviour. Slides worth studying include the India user growth slide, which uses a single large italic statement with a line of supporting numbers, and the smartphone share slide, which places a stacked chart beside a dual-axis chart. The deck is long, and the text provided runs only to slide 107.

## Questions about this deck

**How many slides does the Mary Meeker, Kleiner Perkins Internet Trends 2016 deck have?**

The deck has 214 pages, but the text provided only runs to slide 107. The summary notes the deck is long, so the full 214 pages were not all reviewed here.

**What does the Kleiner Perkins Internet Trends 2016 deck say about India's internet users?**

Slide 8 states that India's growth is accelerating at +40% vs. +33% Y/Y, with 277MM users, and that India passed the USA to become the #2 global user market behind China. Slide 9 repeats 277MM users at 22% penetration.

**What does Mary Meeker of Kleiner Perkins say about global smartphone unit shipments?**

Slide 10 is titled Global Smartphone Unit Shipments Slowing Dramatically at +10% vs. +28% Y/Y. Slide 13 gives the 2015 share as iOS = 16% and Android = 81%.

**How is the Kleiner Perkins Internet Trends 2016 deck structured?**

Slide 3 lists an eight-part outline: global internet trends, global macro trends, advertising, commerce and brand trends, re-imagining communication (video, image, messaging), re-imagining human-computer interfaces (voice, transportation), China, public and private company data, and data as a platform with data privacy.

**Layout**

Full-width navy header band across the top carrying a two-line left-aligned title at the top margin. Below it, a left column holds the chart heading centred above a radar chart with its legend at the upper right of the chart, and a right column of five stacked cards (groups 1 to 5, top to bottom) spans from about 17% to 88% of the height. Footer runs along the bottom: logo at the left margin, source line beside it, and right-aligned footer text with the page number at the right margin; no slide number other than the footer text.

**Visuals**

Chart: radar (spider) chart with four axes meeting at the top (Incentives), right (Low incomes and affordability), bottom (User capability) and left (Infrastructure); radial scale 0 to 100 with rings labelled 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100 along the top axis; no units. Five series, values about (estimated from the drawing, not printed): Group 1 about Incentives 20, Low incomes 33, User capability 37, Infrastructure 34 (light blue line); Group 2 about Incentives 35, Low incomes 71, User capability 83, Infrastructure 34 (light periwinkle line); Group 3 about Incentives 32, Low incomes 75, User capability 88, Infrastructure 42 (mid blue line); Group 4 about Incentives 43, Low incomes 64, User capability 90, Infrastructure 48 (navy line); Group 5 about Incentives 68, Low incomes 91, User capability 99, Infrastructure 86 (black line). No values are printed on the points; the file also contains a hidden black text '3' at 4.44% size near the lower left of the chart that is not visible in the render. Legend at upper right of chart listing Group 1 to Group 5 with line swatches in the same colours as the series. Highlighted points: none. Icons: four navy circular icons, one above Incentives (monitor with globe and running figure), one left of Infrastructure (two gears), one right of Low incomes (banknote with dollar sign), one below User capability (head profile with gears). Right column: five cards, each with a bitmap drop shadow, a light grey body and a coloured header band, each listing groups' countries, offline population 2014 and internet penetration 2014 as in the text. Footer logo: @KPCB wordmark in green-teal letters at lower left.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. White background. Header band in dark teal-navy #00517A with a thin cyan #02B5CC accent line below it. Title in white regular Arial-type sans-serif (ArialMT), about 3.3% of slide height, single weight. Chart heading in bold black Arial, about 2.2%. Axis and category labels: category names in bold cyan #02B5CC about 2.2%; tick labels bold black about 1.8%. Left-column notes in navy #002960, regular Arial about 1.7%, with the first line bold. Card headers in bold Arial about 1.5%: group 1 header text black on pale blue #C7E0FB, group 2 black on periwinkle #91B0FF, group 3 white on blue #0066CC, group 4 white on navy #002960, group 5 white on black #000000. Card body labels bold navy #002960 and values regular black, about 1.5%. Card bodies #F8F8F8 with soft drop shadows; square corners. Chart plot area #F8F8F8 with light grey gridlines. Source line regular black about 0.9%. Footer text regular grey #A6AAA9 about 1.5%.

America 28% (green), Japan 13% (pale mint), China 11% (red), Emerging Asia ex-China 7% (cyan), Lat Am 9% (yellow), Middle East Africa Other 9% (dark blue). Crimson outline arc encloses the N. America + Europe + Japan slices (labelled 63% of Total); blue outline arc encloses the China + Emerging Asia slices (labelled 18% of Total). 2015 pie (large, about 57.4% to 88.3% of width, 39.7% to 79.7% of height): Europe 15% (purple, top right), N. America 13% (green), Japan 1% (pale mint, leader line to label), China 37% (red, bottom), Emerging Asia ex-China 26% (cyan, left), Lat Am 0% (yellow, leader line, sliver), Middle East Africa Other 9% (dark blue, top left). Slices are separated by small white gaps; the N. America + Europe + Japan group is pulled slightly outward and outlined in crimson, the China + Emerging Asia group is outlined in blue. Labels in the 2015 pie are white bold inside the slices and black outside. Legend below the charts: colour squares with Europe (purple), N. America (green), Japan (pale mint), China (red), Emerging Asia (ex-China) (cyan), Lat Am (yellow), Middle East, Africa, Other (dark blue). No data axes; values are printed on the slices.

**Layout**

Two-column timeline on a white page. A full-width dark teal title band sits across the top, with a thin teal rule beneath it. The left column (about x 12 to 40%) holds a bold heading and two stacked circular year markers joined by a dotted arrow. The right column (x 46 to 87.5%) holds two photographs stacked vertically, each joined to its year marker by a horizontal dotted line. The source line sits bottom-left beside the @KPCB logo, and the footer text sits bottom-right. No slide number is shown apart from 'PAGE 25' in the footer.

**Visuals**

Two photographs and two circular year markers with connectors. Photo 1 (top right, 1987): a hazy daytime panorama over the Huangpu River taken from an elevated viewpoint. Many small boats and larger ships sit on grey-blue water, a dense low-rise urban grid fills the middle distance, and a historic clock tower and domed building with a red-roofed ship at the right edge are visible. Overcast pale blue sky fills the top half, and the image is a full rectangle with no border. Photo 2 (lower right, 2016): a clear-sky daytime view of the Pudong skyline across the river, showing the Oriental Pearl Tower with its spheres and spire at left-centre, a cluster of high-rise towers, the tall glass Shanghai Tower at right with a Jin Mao-style tower nearby, and river boats in the foreground. Overall tone is saturated cyan-blue sky and teal-grey water, with a small historic building with a clock tower at the bottom right. Both photographs are plain rectangles, not cropped to shape, with no overlay or tint. Year markers: a grey filled circle labelled 1987 and a teal filled circle labelled 2016, each with a dotted grey connector running right to its photo. A grey dotted vertical line runs from the 1987 circle to the 2016 circle, ending in a small grey downward-pointing solid triangle just above the 2016 circle. Logo: a small green '@KPCB' wordmark at bottom-left.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Clean corporate style on a white page. Title band is dark teal #00517A with a thin bright teal rule #02B5CC along its lower edge. Title text is white regular Arial-style sans-serif, about 4.4% of slide height, left-aligned. Heading 'Shanghai, China, Pudong District' is bold black Arial (Helvetica-like sans-serif), about 3.3% of slide height, centre-aligned. Year labels are white bold sans-serif, about 3.3%. Body text black #000000 regular at about 0.9% for the source line. Footer text is light grey #A6AAA9 regular sans-serif about 1.5%. Accent colours: grey #7F8F92 for the 1987 marker and vertical arrow, teal #02B5CC for the 2016 marker. Connectors are grey dotted lines. Shapes are flat with no shadows, gradients or rounded corners beyond fully round circles.

**Layout**

Full-width dark blue title band across the top with two white title lines left-aligned at the left margin (about 2% from the left edge), a thin teal rule beneath it, then a centred bold chart heading. The chart occupies the centre-left as three stacked bar columns (Q4:00, Q4:07, Q2:15) with row labels in the middle, and a right-hand table of compound annual growth ovals; a bottom row holds total debt and GDP growth ovals. Source line bottom-left beside the KPCB logo, and the footer text with page number 31 bottom-right.

**Visuals**

Chart: stacked column chart, titled 'Global Debt By Type ($T, Constant 2014 FX), Q4:00 – Q2:15'. Y-axis not drawn; values are printed on segments in $ trillions. Three columns with category labels Q4:00, Q4:07, Q2:15 beneath. Column totals printed above: $84 (Q4:00), $138 (Q4:07), $208 (Q2:15). Segments from bottom to top in every column: Financial (grey #B2B2B2), Government (red #C82055), Corporate (blue #00689D), Household (green #31AF78). Q4:00 values: Financial $20, Government $21, Corporate $25, Household $19. Q4:07 values: Financial $37, Government $32, Corporate $37, Household $33. Q2:15 values: Financial $49, Government $59, Corporate $59, Household $41. Annotation: a dark blue oval badge reading '+70T' sits above the Q4:07 column; a black arrow with thin dashed guide lines runs vertically from the top of the Q4:07 column ($138) up to the top of the Q2:15 column ($208). Row labels to the right of the Q2:15 column in black sans-serif: Household, Corporate, Government, Financial, aligned to segment rows. Right-hand table 'Compound annual growth rate (%)' with a black underline and two sub-columns '2000–2007' and '2007–Q2:15' each underlined. Ovals with white bold values: Household 8.5 and 3.0 (green #31AF78); Corporate 5.7 and 6.4 (blue #00689D); Government 5.9 and 8.7 (red #C82055); Financial 9.6 and 3.7 (grey #B2B2B2). Bottom row: 'Total debt as % of GDP' label with blue glossy oval badges 250 (Q4:00), 274 (Q4:07), 299 (Q2:15) with white bold numbers and a subtle dark drop shadow. 'GDP Growth*:' label underlined with yellow (#F5B800) oval badges 4.1 and 2.2 in white bold numbers. Logo: '@KPCB' green pixel-style wordmark bottom-left. No photographs.

**Design**

Background white. Title band solid dark teal-blue #00517A with a thin cyan rule #00A6B4 beneath it. Title text white regular Arial/Helvetica sans-serif, about 3.9% of slide height per line, two lines. Chart heading and column totals in bold black Arial, about 3.0% (heading) and 2.2% (labels) of slide height. Row labels in regular black Arial about 2.6%. Segment and oval values in bold white Arial about 2.2%. Accent colours: green #31AF78, blue #00689D, red #C82055, grey #B2B2B2, yellow #F5B800, dark teal #00517A. Shapes are flat rectangles for bars and rounded ellipses for ovals; no corner radii on bars; oval badges have soft shadows only on the total-debt ovals. Footer text light grey #A6AAA9 regular, about 1.5% of slide height; source notes black regular about 0.9%.

5 Epic Growth Drivers Over Past 2 Decades =
Losing Mojo
1) Connectivity Growth Slowing –
Internet Users rose to 3B from 35MM (1995)

Underdeveloped regions developed – including China / Emerging Asia /
Middle East which rose to 69% of global GDP growth from 43%...
3) Government Debt Rising (& High) –
Spending rose to help support growth...Government debt-to-GDP

4) Interest Rates Have Declined –

5) Population Growth Rate Slowing & Population Aging –

continued to fall – to 1.2% from 1.6% (1995)

Full-width dark teal header band across the top about 12.5% of the slide height with the two-line white title left-aligned at about 2.1% from the left edge; below it a centred bold chart title, a legend row centred above the plot, and a single bar chart with the y-axis title rotated on the left and category labels along the baseline. A callout box sits at the right of the plot and a footer row at the bottom holds the @KPCB logo at the left, the source note in the centre-left and the running footer text at the right. **Visuals**

Chart: clustered column chart titled '% of Time Spent in Media vs. % of Advertising Spending, USA, 2015'. Y axis titled '% of Total Media Consumption Time or Advertising Spending', units percent, range 0% to 50% with gridlines every 10%. X categories Print, Radio, TV, Internet, Mobile. Two series: Time Spent (yellow #FCD03F) with labelled values Print 4%, Radio 13%, TV 36%, Internet 22%, Mobile 25%; Ad Spend (teal #02B5CC) with labelled values Print 16%, Radio 10%, TV 39%, Internet 23%, Mobile 12%. Mobile Ad Spend bar has a pale mint (#D2F2E4) unlabelled extension from 12% up to 25% representing the opportunity. Legend at top: yellow square Time Spent, teal square Ad Spend. Arrow icons: light blue gradient block arrows with tan outline: down arrows above Print Ad Spend and Print Time Spent, two down arrows above TV Time Spent and TV Ad Spend; up arrows above Mobile Time Spent and the Mobile opportunity area; stacked flat markers (pairs of short light blue bars with tan outline) above Radio bars and above Internet bars. Logo: @KPCB wordmark in green at bottom left. No photographs.

**Layout**

A full-width dark teal title band runs across the top 12.5% of the slide, with the two-line title left-aligned in white at about x 2.1%. **Visuals**

Four photographs sit above the column headers, each boxed with square corners and no border, not cropped to a shape. (1) Silent column: black-and-white photograph of a sailor embracing and kissing a woman in a white dress on a city street with a crowd of onlookers in the background; grey tones, overcast daylight, medium-wide framing, subject in the centre-left. (2) Baby Boomers column: black-and-white studio portrait of four young men in dark suits and ties posed close together against a plain grey backdrop, lit softly from the front, head-and-shoulders framing. (3) Gen X column: colour photograph of six people posed together in casual clothes against a blue-grey backdrop with warm orange light at the upper right; dominant colours are blue, orange and black. (4) Millennials column: colour photograph of about twelve people crowded around a restaurant or home dinner table, smiling at the camera, warm yellow interior lighting, dominant colours brown, red and dark green; framed inside the red dashed outline. A red dashed rectangle (#E0202A, about 3 pt dashes) outlines the entire Millennials column from the header down to the Financial Approach row, with no fill. The table has light grey #D9D9D9 hairline cell borders. The @KPCB logo at bottom left is a green pixel-style wordmark with an ‘@’ symbol before ‘KPCB’, colour about #2EB872.

Source: Pew Research / Image: Doomsteaddiner.net, Billboard.com, Metro.co.uk / Note: *Only shows those that were civilian employed (i.e. excludes armed forces, unemployed civilians, and those not in labor force). **Median household income shown in 2015 dollars. Pew Research Center tabulations of the March Current Population Surveys (1963, 1980, 1998, and 2014). Pew Research defines each generation and may differ from other sources as there are varying opinions on what years each generation begin and end.

**Layout**

Full-width dark teal title band across the top with a two-line left-aligned title. Below it a four-column comparison table with a row-label column at the left, photographs centred above each generation column, and the Millennials column boxed by a red dashed outline. Source notes sit bottom-left, the KPCB logo bottom-left corner and the footer with page number bottom-right, all with about 2% margins.

**Visuals**

Table with four data columns (Silent, Baby Boomers, Gen X, Millennials) and nine data rows plus a header row. Row labels in the left column: Birth Years; Year Most of Generation 18-33 Years Old; Location When Ages 18-33 Metropolitan as % Total; Diversity When Ages 18-33 White as % Total; Marital Status When Ages 18-33 Married as % Total; Education by Gender When Ages 18-33 % with Bachelor's Degree; Employment Status by Gender When Ages 18-33 Employed as % Total*; Median Household Income ** When Ages 18-33; Population of Generation When Ages 18-33. Values by column: Birth Years 1928 – 1945 | 1946 – 1964 | 1965 – 1980 | 1981 – 1996. Year Most 1963 | 1980 | 1998 | 2014. Location 64% | 68% | 83% | 86%. Diversity 84% | 77% | 66% | 57%. Marital 64% | 49% | 38% | 28%. Education 12% Male / 7% Female | 17% Male / 14% Female | 18% Male / 20% Female | 21% Male / 27% Female. Employment 78% Male / 38% Female | 78% Male / 60% Female | 78% Male / 69% Female | 68% Male / 63% Female. Median Income N/A | $61,115 | $64,469 | $62,066. Population 35MM | 61MM | 60MM | 68MM. Four photographs above the header row: Silent photo is a black-and-white street scene of a sailor in a white uniform and cap embracing and kissing a woman in a white dress, with onlookers and buildings behind, cropped to a landscape rectangle, boxed, no overlay. Baby Boomers photo is a black-and-white studio portrait of four young men in dark suits and ties, close together, plain grey backdrop, soft even front lighting, landscape rectangle boxed. Gen X photo is a colour publicity-style group portrait of six people posed close together against a blue-grey backdrop with warm orange and brown tones, lit evenly, boxed. Millennials photo is a colour snapshot of about fifteen young adults crowded around a restaurant table with bottles and food, warm indoor tungsten light, a pendant lamp above, boxed. A red dashed rectangle outlines the entire Millennials column from the photo down to the population row. KPCB logo: green stylised wordmark '@KPCB' at bottom-left.

**Design**

Background white. Title band fill #00517A with a thin lighter teal rule beneath it, about #1AA5B5, about 0.8% of slide height. Title text white #FFFFFF, Arial-like regular sans-serif, about 3.7% of slide height. Table header labels bold black #000000 Arial-like sans-serif, about 2.2% of slide height. Body and row text black #000000 Arial-like sans-serif, about 1.5% of slide height. Row labels bold with italic sub-labels. Footer text grey #A6AAA9, about 1.5%. Source note black, about 0.9%. Table fills #F2F2F2 for header row and label column, white for data cells, thin light grey #D9D9D9 cell borders. Red dashed outline #E8202A, about 0.5% stroke weight, square corners. No shadows or gradients.

Below it a centred bold black subtitle sits at about 22% height over a timeline grid: a full-width teal Generational Overlap bar, five staggered generation bars stepping diagonally from lower left to upper right, then twelve decade columns of equal width (about 8.3% each) with teal year headers and stacked logos in five rows, separated by thin grey vertical rules. The footer has the @KPCB logo at lower left, a small source and note block centred-left, and a right-aligned running footer with page number 57 at the bottom right.

Diagram/timeline. Twelve decade columns labelled 1900s, 1910s, 1920s, 1930s, 1940s, 1950s, 1960s, 1970s, 1980s, 1990s, 2000s, 2010s. Below it five generation bars, each a dark blue (#00689D) chevron-ended label bar on a light grey (#F2F2F2) chevron track running to the right edge: GI Generation (starts at 1900s, ends near 1920s), Silent Generation (starts 1920s, ends near 1940s), Baby Boomers (starts 1940s, ends near 1960s), Generation X (starts 1960s, ends near 1980s), Millennials (starts 1980s, ends near 1990s/2000s), Generation Z (starts near 2000s, extends to right edge). Two vertical bar charts. Left chart: type vertical column chart; title 'Population by Age Range, USA, 2014'; y-axis titled 'USA Population (MM)', range 0 to 70 with gridlines every 10 (units millions); x-axis categories '<15', '15 to 24', '25 to 34', '35 to 44', '45 to 54', '55 to 64', '65 to 74', '>75'; one series with no printed data labels, so values are estimates: <15 about 61 MM; 15 to 24 about 43.7 MM; 25 to 34 about 42.0 MM; 35 to 44 about 40.8 MM; 45 to 54 about 44.3 MM; 55 to 64 about 38.6 MM; 65 to 74 about 23.8 MM; >75 about 19.3 MM. Bars 15 to 24 and 25 to 34 are light green #33B780 and all others are blue #00689D; a green bracket above the two green bars is labelled 'Millennials'. No legend. Right chart: type vertical column chart; title 'Household Expenditure, Annual Average, by Age of Reference Person, USA, 2014'; y-axis titled 'Annual Expenditure ($K)', range $0 to $70 with gridlines every $10 (units thousands of dollars); x-axis categories '<25', '25 to 34', '35 to 44', '45 to 54', '55 to 64', '65 to 74', '>75'; no printed values, so estimates: <25 about $32.1K; 25 to 34 about $49.5K; 35 to 44 about $62.5K; 45 to 54 about $65.7K; 55 to 64 about $56.2K; 65 to 74 about $48.8K; >75 about $36.7K. The 25 to 34 bar and the <25 bar are green #33B780 (Millennial), all others blue #00689D. A large right-pointing block arrow runs diagonally up and to the right across the chart from above the <25 bar to above the 35 to 44 bar, filled light mint #E4F8EF with a green #33B780 outline, with the rotated label 'Millennials' in green bold on it. A small white rectangle sits behind the arrow's label. Logo: the '@KPCB' wordmark in the bottom-left, a 72 by 25 pixel green bitmap logo. No photographs or icons.

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF background with the dark blue #00517A title band across the top. Clean corporate data slide. Title band is solid dark blue #00517A across the full top edge, about 12.5% of slide height, with a thin cyan-teal rule #1CB5C6 along its bottom edge about 0.6% tall. ### Slide 64

**Text**

...Products Become Brands...Brands Become Retailers... / Retailers Become Products / Brands...Retailers Come Into Homes... / Less differentiation between products / brands / retailers as single products evolve into brands + consumers shop directly from / brands + retailers leverage insights to develop own vertically-integrated brands...New distribution models emerging enabling / direct-to-consumer commerce in the home... / Products → / Brands / (Casper) / Brands → / Retailers / (Warby Parker) / Retailers → / Products / Brands / (Thrive Market) / New DTC / Distribution Models / (Stitch Fix) / Image: Myjane.ru, CNBC.com, Vanityfair.com, Insidebusinessnyc.com, Funandfit.org, Thrivemarket.com, Thedustyrosestyle.com, Stitchfix.tumblr.com / KPCB INTERNET TRENDS 2016 | PAGE 63

**Layout**

Full-width dark blue title band across the top with a two-line white title left-aligned near the top margin, then a centred italic subtitle paragraph beneath it. Below, four columns sit side by side: three equal-width columns (Products to Brands, Brands to Retailers, Retailers to Products/Brands) separated by faint dashed vertical guides and connected by grey block arrows, then a heavy black vertical divider and a red dashed box framing the fourth column (New DTC Distribution Models). Each column has a bold centred heading with a bold-italic-free name in parentheses, one photo at the top and one photo in the lower half. Source line at bottom left beside a small green @KPCB logo; page label at bottom right, right-aligned.

**Visuals**

Eight photographs and one logo. Column 1 top: photo of a white bed with pillows and a teal throw in a bright room, with an open striped Casper cardboard box standing beside it; soft neutral light, light grey walls, warm wood floor; boxed, rectangular, not cropped. Column 1 bottom: photo of a subway platform wall with a row of illuminated blue backlit advertising panels reading BETTER SLEEP FOR ALL, Casper and CASPER.COM, with some white and purple panels at right; dark blue and purple dominant colours with warm tiled wall; boxed, not cropped. Column 2 top: studio photo on a white background of about six pairs of sunglasses (dark tortoiseshell red-brown frames and black frames) scattered at angles with soft shadows; boxed-free, cut out on white. Column 2 bottom: photo of a bright Warby Parker retail store interior with white glass display tables, shelves of eyewear on both walls and a dark wooden central display; white and light grey with warm wood accents; boxed, not cropped. Column 3 top: overhead photo on a saturated blue background of Thrive Market products (granola bars, nut bars and almonds) with a centred white THRIVE MARKET logo and the text WHOLESOME PRODUCTS. WHOLESALE PRICES. and ThriveMarket.com; boxed square. Column 3 bottom: studio photo on white of a white plastic jar of Thrive Market COCONUT OIL with a green leaf-pattern label, white lid and small print; boxed, not cropped. Column 4 top: photo of an open pale-green patterned Stitch Fix shipping box with tissue paper, a folded note reading WHAT TO DO NEXT and a round mint logo sticker, sitting on a beige fur rug on tiles; warm light; boxed, not cropped. Column 4 bottom: studio photo on white of six mannequins in blue and pink dresses and skirts with scarves and necklaces, arranged in two rows of three; saturated royal blue, hot pink and white; cut out on white. Footer logo: green @KPCB wordmark in a bold rounded sans, small, at bottom left.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF, with the dark blue #00517A header band across the top. White #FFFFFF slide background with a dark teal-blue header band #00517A and a thin lighter teal rule #1AA3A3 beneath it. Title text is white #FFFFFF in a regular-weight Arial-like sans-serif at about 4.1% of slide height. Subtitle and column headings are black #000000; headings are bold Arial, subtitle is Arial italic at about 2.2%. Column heading parentheticals are regular Arial. Source line is black regular Arial at about 0.9%. Footer page label is light grey #A6AAA9 regular Arial at about 1.5%. Accents: black vertical divider #000000, red dashed frame #E02020, grey arrows #C8C8C8, faint grey dashed guides #D0D0D0. Thin straight line weights; no corner radii, shadows or gradients; photographs are plain rectangles with no borders.

**Layout**

Full-width dark blue title band across the top with two white title lines left-aligned at the left margin. Below it, three equal columns separated by thin vertical grey rules at about 33 percent and 66 percent of the width, each with a bold centred heading. Left column stacks product photos, a video call still and a phone screenshot; centre column stacks a phone screenshot with a dashed highlight, and a doorbell video still; right column stacks three map images with blue date labels. Footer has the @KPCB logo at lower left with a source line beside it, and the right-aligned footer text 'KPCB INTERNET TRENDS 2016 | PAGE 65' at lower right.

**Visuals**

Left column: (1) a product photograph on white showing a black Ring Stick Up camera mounted on a black bracket at left and a silver Ring doorbell at right, each with a soft grey floor shadow. (2) A video call still: a man with short brown hair and a grey hoodie looking at the camera, framed by a white circular fisheye border, outdoor street with trees, cars and blue sky behind, bottom bar dark with red END CALL button, full-colour, boxed rectangle. (3) A phone screenshot of the Ring 'My Plan' screen on a light grey background, blue status and header bar, three device thumbnails with green checkmarks and red REMOVE links (Front Door, Side 2, Side 1), grey Monthly tile and white Yearly tile with checkmark, SUMMARY box showing 3 active devices and $90.00. Centre column: (4) a green-headered phone screenshot of a Nextdoor General thread with two posts, the second post enclosed by an orange dashed rectangle, and a bottom navigation bar with Home, Inbox, Notifications (highlighted green), Neighbors and More icons. (5) A fisheye doorbell camera still of a man in dark clothing carrying a package up a porch, with a WLKY news logo lower right and 'ring.com' watermark lower left. Right column: three map tiles of New York region in greyscale street-map style with blue water, showing density of small coloured square dots: April 2015 sparse mostly green-yellow dots; December 2015 denser green dots in a band across the coast; May 2016 very dense dots shifting from green to yellow to red with the red concentration over Long Island and Brooklyn. No axes, no legend, no values printed.

**Design**

Background: White (#FFFFFF) background with a dark blue #00517A header band across the top. **Layout**

Full-width dark teal title band across the top with a two-line white title left-aligned at about 2 percent from the left edge; below it four equal columns separated by thin vertical grey rules, each column with a bold centred heading, a dotted rule, a bold italic centred subtitle with year, three centred body items and a visual near the bottom. Footer runs along the bottom: KPCB logo and small source lines at left, grey running head and printed page number at right. No slide number is printed beyond the footer text 'PAGE 76'.

**Visuals**

Four columns of visuals. Column 1 (Live (Linear)): one black-and-white photograph of a mid-century family (a woman, a man and several children) seated on a sofa watching a boxed vintage television with a rounded screen in a living room; boxed, rectangular, not cropped. Column 2 (On-Demand): a black Tivo DVR set-top box lying horizontally on a white background with its black remote control resting diagonally on top and a faint reflection below; and below it a solid red rectangle with the Netflix wordmark 'NETFLIX' in black capitals with a white outline-like edge centred on it. Column 3 (Semi-Live): a vertical selfie photograph, warm brown and yellow tones, of two smiling young men cheek to cheek, the man on the left in a grey shirt and the man on the right with dark hair; a translucent dark caption band at the bottom reads 'Playoff beards! Go Sharks / Warriors!!' in white. Column 4 (Real-Live): two vertical phone screenshots side by side. Left screenshot (Periscope): a photo of three women in a park with sunglasses and a city skyline behind, white text 'Sunny day!!' top left, a small 'BROADCAST NOW' pill at top, a red 'Start Broadcast' button, and a grey on-screen keyboard below. Right screenshot (Facebook Live): a photo of a smiling bald man in sunglasses surrounded by a crowd, a red 'Live' badge reading '15,934 Viewers', a comment list in white text, a 'Kevin Hart joined.' notice, and a 'Write a comment...' field with 'Post' at bottom right on a black band. Logo at bottom left: green '@KPCB' wordmark.

**Design**

Background white. Title band fill #00517A (dark teal blue) with white titles (#FFFFFF) in Arial regular, title text about 4.4 percent of slide height. Thin cyan rule under band approx #1BB5C9. Column headings in Arial Bold black #000000, about 3.2 percent of slide height. Subtitles in Arial Bold Italic black #000000 about 2.2 percent. Body text Arial regular black #000000 about 2.2 percent. Dividers light grey #D9D9D9 thin solid; dotted separators grey #BFBFBF. Footer source text black about 0.9 percent; running head grey #A6AAA9 about 1.5 percent. Logo green approx #2BB673. Photos have no border, no shadow, square corners.

**Layout**

Two equal columns separated by a thin vertical divider at about x 49.7%, running from about y 16% to y 91%. Source line sits bottom-left beside the @KPCB logo; the footer text and page number sit bottom-right in grey.

**Visuals**

Two images. (1) Left column, a photograph of a hand holding a silver iPhone in portrait orientation, boxed with straight edges and no rounded corners, not cropped. The phone screen shows a living room in View In My Room mode with a bright red sofa placed on a striped floor, a chandelier and windows; the screen has Cancel and Save buttons at the top and Text and Color tools at the bottom. A second hand's fingertip touches the screen. Soft natural daylight, bright white and pale grey tones, with a red sofa as the single saturated accent. (2) Right column, a screenshot of a black iPad in landscape orientation with a dark bezel, shown full width of its box with a rounded device outline. The screen shows a kitchen with dark navy base cabinets, pendant lights, open shelving, a stone countertop, a wooden floor and white window shutters. Yellow-green handwritten-style sketch annotations read 'Storage idea' with a downward arrow pointing at a hanging pan rack, and 'Add bar stools' near the bottom; two white outline sketches of bar stools are drawn in front of the cabinets. Left-side tool icons are visible in a dark vertical strip. Warm and neutral tones with yellow-green annotation colour. No charts or tables.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF with the full-width dark teal header band #00517A across the top 12.5%. White background with a dark teal header band (#00517A) and a thin cyan rule beneath it. Title text is white ArialMT regular, about 4.4% of slide height (roughly 6.5% for capitals). **Layout**

Full-width dark teal title band across the top (about 12.5% of slide height) with two left-aligned white title lines starting at about 2% left margin. Below it, a single line chart fills the centre, with a centred bold chart title, the y-axis title rotated at the left, year labels along the bottom, direct series labels at the right edge and a horizontal legend row above the footer. The footer has the KPCB logo and source/note lines at bottom left and a grey running footer with page number at bottom right.

**Visuals**

Line chart. Title: Monthly Active Users on Select Social Networks and Messengers, Global, 2011 – 2015. Y-axis: Monthly Active Users (MM), range 0 to 1,200, gridlines and labels at 0, 200, 400, 600, 800, 1,000, 1,200. X-axis: years 2011 to 2015, one tick per year. Series (no values are printed; estimates given): LinkedIn (slate grey #46525E): 2012 about 58, 2013 about 78, 2014 about 95, 2015 about 100; starts 2012. Twitter (light yellow #FBD97A): 2011 about 117, 2012 about 190, 2013 about 245, 2014 about 290, 2015 about 305. Instagram (magenta #C93B6E): 2011 about 15, 2012 about 100, 2013 about 200, 2014 about 300, 2015 about 400. WhatsApp (green #3DB87A): 2013 about 450, 2014 about 700, 2015 about 1,000. WeChat (red #E03A24): 2012 about 160, 2013 about 355, 2014 about 500, 2015 about 700. Facebook Messenger (blue #0064D2): 2013 about 200, 2014 about 500, 2015 about 800. Legend: horizontal row of six coloured line swatches with labels LinkedIn, Twitter, Instagram, WhatsApp, WeChat, Facebook Messenger, in bold black. End-of-line callouts at right: WhatsApp Launched 2010; Facebook Messenger (2011); WeChat (2011); Instagram (2010); Twitter (2006); LinkedIn (2003), each name in bold with the year in italic. No highlighted points. Logo: green pixelated @KPCB wordmark at bottom left, about 72 by 25 px, colour about #3DB87A.

**Design**

Background white. Title band is solid #00517A with a thin bright cyan rule #1BB5C5 along its lower edge. Title and subtitle text white #FFFFFF in Arial regular, about 4.4% of slide height per line, left aligned. Chart title and axis labels are Arial bold black #000000 about 2.6% to 3.0% of slide height. Series labels are Arial bold black 1.8% with italic year lines. Legend labels Arial bold black about 2.2%. Source and note text Arial regular black about 0.9%. Running footer Arial regular grey #A6AAA9 about 1.5%. Lines are about 3 px wide, round caps, no markers. Gridlines are hairline light grey #E5E5E5. No shadows, no gradients, no corner radii.

**Layout**

A full-width dark teal title band fills the top 12.5 percent of the slide, with a thin cyan rule beneath it; the two-line white title is left-aligned at about a 2 percent left margin. Below, a single table runs from about x 24 percent to x 94 percent: row labels in a left column (x 24 percent), then three value columns centred at about x 47.5, 66.2 and 85.2 percent, with logos in a header row at y 15 to 23 percent. Two boxed section labels sit at the left (x 6 percent): 'New Services Added 2015 -16*' at y 37.5 to 44.4 percent and 'Previous Existing Services' at y 62 to 69 percent. The footer has the KPCB logo at bottom left, a three-line source and note block starting at x 10.5 percent, and a right-aligned running footer with the page number at bottom right.

Table with 3 header rows and 17 body rows. Columns: row label, KakaoTalk, WeChat, LINE. **Layout**

Two equal columns split by a thin vertical grey divider at about 51% of the width, with a full-width title band across the top. Each column has a bold heading, a regular subtitle line, a phone screenshot, and an italic two-line caption block, all centred within the column. The title sits left-aligned in the header band with about 2% side margins. The footer has the KPCB logo at bottom left, a two-line source note beside it, and the running footer with page number 104 at bottom right.

**Visuals**

Two photographs of phone screens showing Facebook Messenger conversations, both shown as boxed flat screenshots with no crop, no overlay and no tint. Left screenshot (Hyatt, 9:07 PM, AT&T status bar, Typically replies within an hour, Manage button): a partial blue bubble reading 'through Thursday?', then grey bubble 'The Grand Hyatt as 2 double beds for $429 per night or one king for $459 per night, the Hyatt Regency has two double beds or one king for $604 per night plus tax. Would you like to book one of those hotels? ^LM' (timestamp WED 7:50 PM, Hyatt avatar), blue bubble 'Which one has better parking options?' (WED 8:29 PM), grey bubble 'Hyatt Regency valet is at $67/ night tax inclusive. Grand Hyatt is the same at $67/tax inclusive. ^as' (WED 8:46 PM, Hyatt avatar), blue bubble 'Thanks!', message field 'Message Hyatt...' with icon row. Right screenshot (Rogers, 10:26 AM, ROGERS carrier, 85% battery, Typically replies in minutes, Block button, date APR 14, 6:25 PM): blue bubbles 'Hello my internet is down.' and 'I'm at', grey bubble 'Hi thanks for reaching out to us. I'm sorry your internet is down. I can definitely look in to this for you. Do you have your account number handy or a phone number linked to your account? Alicia' with red Rogers avatar, a blank blue bubble, blue bubble 'Looks like it just came back up', grey bubble 'Thank you Joshua. Unfortunately there is an outage in your area right now. I apologize for the inconvenience. We are working to have the service back up and running as soon as possible our estimated time is about 3 hours. Alicia', blue bubble 'Ok looks ok at the moment but it was ouat earlier.', and a partly cut-off grey bubble 'That is great to hear! Is there anything else I can assist you with today? Alicia' with message field 'Message Rogers...' and icon row. Both screenshots are white/light grey with blue (#0A84FF-like) outgoing bubbles and light grey (#EFEFEF-like) incoming bubbles. KPCB logo: green (#2DB26B-like) wordmark '@KPCB' in a heavy condensed sans.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Clean white content area under a dark teal header band. Title text is white regular sans-serif (Arial-like) at about 4.3% of slide height, body and subtitles are black Arial regular at about 2.2%, bold column headings are black Arial Bold at about 3.0%, captions are black Arial Italic at about 2.2%. Footer text is grey #A6AAA9 Arial at about 1.5%, source notes are black Arial at about 0.9%. A thin teal (#1AA7B5-like) rule sits along the bottom edge of the header band. The vertical divider is a light grey (#D0D0D0-like) hairline. No shadows, gradients or rounded shapes apart from the rounded phone-screen bubbles inside the screenshots.

**Layout**

Full-width title band at the top with a three-line-free table below: a header row of seven teal cells and three body rows (WeChat, Facebook, Line), with the first column holding app logos and the row labels, separated by thin grey rules. Title is left-aligned in the dark band with a 2% left margin; the table spans about 6% to 94% of the width and sits in the middle of the slide with empty space above and below. Footer has the KPCB logo bottom-left, a small source line beside it, and a right-aligned running footer with the page number printed as 105.

**Visuals**

Table with seven columns and three data rows plus header row. Header columns: blank (logo column), Business / Official Accounts, Engagement, Payments, B2C Chat for SMEs, Advertising (Within Messengers), Partnerships / Other Services. Row 1 WeChat: logo; 10MM+ Official Accounts; ~80% Users Follow Official Accounts; WeChat Pay (2013); Official Accounts (2012); Official Accounts (2012); Weidian (2014). Row 2 Facebook: Facebook Messenger logo with label Facebook above it; 50MM+ Small Business Pages; 1B+ Messages / Month Between Businesses and Users, +2x Y/Y, 80% Businesses Active on Mobile; Payments (2015); Messaging via Pages (2011) and Chatbots Platform (2016); Sponsored Messages (2016); Shopify & Zendesk Partnership (2015 / 2016). Row 3 Line: LINE logo; 2MM+ Line@ + Official Accounts; -- in Engagement; Line Pay (2014); Official Accounts & Line @ (2012 / 2015) and Chatbots Platform (2016); Official Accounts (2012); Commerce / Stores on Line@ (2016). Logos are small square app icons: WeChat icon is a green rounded square with two white speech bubbles and the word WeChat in white at the bottom; Facebook Messenger icon is a blue gradient speech bubble with a white lightning-bolt; LINE icon is a green rounded square with a white speech bubble containing LINE in green. No charts or photographs.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF background with a dark teal #00517A title band across the top 12.5% of the slide. White background with a dark teal header band (#00517A) carrying white sans-serif title text; a bright teal (#02B5CC) strip and teal header cells. Body text is black (#000000) Arial-style sans-serif, bold for key values and regular for descriptors. Title is regular weight, about 4.4% of slide height (cap height roughly 3.1%); body text about 1.8% of slide height; source and footer text very small, about 0.9% and 1.5%. Table rows are separated by light grey hairline rules (about #D9D9D9), no shadows, no rounded corners, no gradients except the blue Messenger logo.

**Layout**

A full-width dark teal header band across the top (0 to 12.5% of height) holds a two-line white left-aligned title starting at about 2% from the left edge. Below, a centred bold subtitle and a centred regular subheading sit above a row of six phone screenshots spanning the width, each with a bold centred caption beneath; the source line sits bottom-left beside the @KPCB logo and the footer and page number sit bottom-right.

**Visuals**

Six smartphone screenshots of a shopper's conversation flow in Thailand, shown left to right as iPhone-style mockups with white bezels. (1) Visit Instagram Shop: Instagram profile page for 'THESIMPLEEVERYTHINGMA...' showing 10k posts, 71.8k followers, 71k following, a green 'Following' button, bio text and a grid of food and beach photos at the bottom. (2) Browse Products: Instagram grid of women's fashion photos, mostly striped and pastel outfits on grey and beige backgrounds. (3) Inquire About Product via Line: Line chat with the messages 'Sawadee ka', 'Queen set' and 'this colour and black colour have to pre order chai mai ka' on a beige chat background, with a reply bubble 'จ้า'. (4) Get Payment Details: Line chat with a red-outlined box around an olive-green 'ACCOUNT FOR PAYMENT' panel listing bank accounts (sob bank, k bank, bangkok bank) and a second red-outlined yellow-highlighted block of Thai text; a red-bordered rectangle also appears in the chat. (5) Confirm Payment: Line chat showing a 'Thank you' sticker, a red-outlined photograph of a payment slip held in a hand, and the bubble 'Transfer laew na ka'. (6) Ship & Track Order: Line chat with a red-outlined address bubble '3C44 วิบเซ็นต์ ชั้น 3 มาบุญครองเซ็นเตอร์ ปทุมวัน กรุงเทพ 10330', the reply 'en467796750th' and 'Thank you na kaaa :)' with a character sticker. Red rectangles are used as highlights in panels 4, 5 and 6.

**Design**

Background: White #FFFFFF solid background, with the header band #00517A across the top. Clean corporate KPCB style: white slide body, teal-blue header band #00517A with a thin lighter cyan rule beneath it (about #1FB5C9). Title text is white regular sans-serif (Arial), about 4.4% of slide height per line. Subtitle heading is bold black Arial about 4.4% of slide height, subheading regular black Arial about 3.0%. Captions are bold black Arial about 2.4%. Footer and page text are light grey #A6AAA9 Arial about 1.5%. Source line is black Arial about 0.9%. Logo is green #2BB673 bold pixel-style 'KPCB' with an '@' prefix. Phone mockups have light grey-white bezels with no shadows; red #E0141E rectangles are drawn as highlight outlines around chat details.

### Slide 115

**Text**

Human-Computer Interaction (1830s – 2015), USA = / Touch 1.0 → Touch 2.0 → Touch 3.0 → Voice / Punch Cards for / Informatics / 1832 / QWERTY / Keyboard / 1872 / Electromechanical / Computer (Z3) / 1941 / Electronic Computer / (ENIAC) / 1943 / Paper Tape Reader / (Harvard Mark I) / 1944 / Mainframe Computers / (IBM SSEC) / 1948 / Trackball / 1952 / Joystick / 1967 / Microcomputers / (IBM Mark-8) / 1974 / Portable Computer / (IBM 5100) / 1975 / Commercial Use of / Window-Based GUI / (Xerox Star) / 1981 / Commercial Use / of Mouse / (Apple Lisa) / 1983 / Commercial Use / of Mobile / Computing / (PalmPilot) / 1996 / Touch + Camera - / based Mobile / Computing / (iPhone 2G) / 2007 / Voice on Mobile / (Siri) / 2011 / Voice on Connected / Ambient Devices / (Amazon Echo) / 2014 / Source: University of Calgary, “History of Computer Interfaces” (Saul Greenberg) / KPCB INTERNET TRENDS 2016 | PAGE / 114

**Layout**

Title sits in a full-width dark teal band across the top (about 12.5% of slide height) with left-aligned two-line title starting at about 2% from the left edge. Below, a loose grid of 17 items in three rows: row 1 has five items, row 2 has five items, and row 3 has six items, all centred under their images with roughly even column spacing; the last two items of row 3 are enclosed in a red dashed rectangle. Source line sits bottom-left beside the KPCB logo; the footer text 'KPCB INTERNET TRENDS 2016 | PAGE' and page number 114 sit bottom-right.

**Visuals**

Seventeen images, each boxed as a rectangle with no crop shape, no overlay and no tint, plus one red dashed rectangle and the KPCB logo. 1) Punch Cards for Informatics (1832): black-and-white scan of a punched-card grid of rectangular holes with printed column letters along top and bottom, white background. 2) QWERTY Keyboard (1872): black-and-white patent-style drawing with 'Fig. 3' label at top showing a keyboard mechanism with typewriter key levers and letters QWERTY, white background. 3) Electromechanical Computer Z3 (1941): black-and-white image of a keyboard with square keys labelled with numbers and letters and a wide space bar at the bottom, white background. 4) Electronic Computer ENIAC (1943): black-and-white photo of a standing man in a suit beside tall rack cabinets, dark tones, full-frame. 5) Paper Tape Reader Harvard Mark I (1944): black-and-white photo of a woman working at a large machine with tall columns and cables, grey tones. 6) Mainframe Computers IBM SSEC (1948): black-and-white photo of a room with a tall dark column, two people seated on sofas before cabinets, ceiling lights. 7) Trackball (1952): black-and-white photo of a large sphere set in a black frame with metal pillars on a light grey background. 8) Joystick (1967): colour photo of a wood-grain box with two joysticks, a cable and a power adaptor on a light grey background. 9) Microcomputers IBM Mark-8 (1974): colour photo of a beige microcomputer with keyboard and small red display, in a glass-fronted display case with pale blue-green tones. 10) Portable Computer IBM 5100 (1975): colour photo of a beige desktop portable with small screen and keyboard, evenly lit, grey background. 11) Commercial Use of Window-Based GUI Xerox Star (1981): black-and-white photo of a monitor showing the word XEROX and a car illustration on screen, keyboard below. 12) Commercial Use of Mouse Apple Lisa (1983): photo of a beige mouse with cable on a light grey background. 13) Commercial Use of Mobile Computing PalmPilot (1996): photo of a dark grey handheld with grey-green screen, buttons below and a stylus lying diagonally. 14) Touch + Camera-based Mobile Computing iPhone 2G (2007): photo of a white and a black iPhone side by side, the black one showing a grid of control icons. 15) Voice on Mobile Siri (2011): photo of a white iPhone showing the Siri interface beside a purple and silver microphone icon with the word Siri, on a pale background. 16) Voice on Connected / Ambient Devices Amazon Echo (2014): photo of a black cylindrical speaker with a blue ring light on top, on a white background. 17) KPCB logo: green pixel-style '@KPCB' wordmark at bottom-left. Red dashed rectangle encloses Voice on Mobile (Siri) and Voice on Connected / Ambient Devices (Amazon Echo), with dashes in red #FF0000, no fill.

**Design**

Background: Plain white #FFFFFF with a dark teal header band #00517A across the top. White background with a solid dark teal header band (#00517A) and a thin bright teal rule (#13A8B8) along its lower edge. Title text is white (#FFFFFF) regular-weight Arial/Helvetica-style sans-serif at about 4.4% of slide height, in sentence case. Body and caption text is black (#000000) Arial regular at about 1.8% of slide height, with years in Arial bold. Source line is black Arial at about 0.9%. Footer text is grey (#A6AAA9) Arial at about 1.5%. KPCB logo is green. Red dashed outline (#FF0000) with square corners. No shadows, no gradients, no rounded corners.

### Slide 118

**Text**

Person to Machine (P2M) Voice Interaction Adoption Keys =
99% Accuracy in Understanding & Meaning + Low Latency
As speech recognition accuracy goes from say 95% to
99%, all of us in the room will go from barely using it
today to using it all the time. Most people
underestimate the difference between 95% and 99%
accuracy – 99% is a game changer...
No one wants to wait 10 seconds for a response. Accuracy, followed by latency, are the two key metrics
for a production speech system...
ANDREW NG, CHIEF SCIENTIST AT BAIDU
KPCB INTERNET TRENDS 2016 | PAGE
117

One line chart titled 'Google Trends, Worldwide, 2008 – 2016'. Type: multi-series line chart. ### Slide 128

**Text**

Hands & Vision-Free Interaction = / Top Reason to Use Voice...@ Home / In Car / On Go / Primary Reasons for Using Voice, / USA, 2016 1 / Primary Setting for Voice Usage, / USA, 2016 2 / 61% / 30% / 24% / 22% / 12% / 1% / Useful when / hands / vision / occupied / Faster / results / Difficulty typing / on certain / devices / They're fun / / cool / To avoid / confusing / menus / Other / 0% / 20% / 40% / 60% / 80% / 43% / 36% / 19% / 3% / Home / Car / On the go / Work / 0% / 10% / 20% / 30% / 40% / 50% / KPCB INTERNET TRENDS 2016 | PAGE / 127 / Source: MindMeld “Intelligent Voice Assistants Research Report – Q1 2016” / Note: Based on survey of n = 1,800 respondents who were smartphone users over the age of 18, half female half male, geographically distributed across the United States. (1) In response to the survey / question stating “Why do you use voice/search commands? Check all that apply.” (2) In response to the survey question stating “Where do you use voice features the most?”

**Layout**

A full-width dark teal title band runs across the top with a two-line left-aligned white title, and below it two horizontal bar charts sit side by side in two equal columns, each with a centred bold heading above it. The footer row carries the small @KPCB logo at lower left, the source and note lines in small type beside it, and the running head 'KPCB INTERNET TRENDS 2016 | PAGE 127' at lower right; the slide number sits at the far right of the footer with the page number on a second line.

**Visuals**

Two horizontal bar charts. Left chart: title 'Primary Reasons for Using Voice, USA, 2016 (superscript 1)'; category axis lists Useful when hands / vision occupied, Faster results, Difficulty typing on certain devices, They're fun / cool, To avoid confusing menus, Other; value axis 0% to 80% in 20% steps, light grey vertical gridlines at each step; labelled values: Useful when hands / vision occupied 61%, Faster results 30%, Difficulty typing on certain devices 24%, They're fun / cool 22%, To avoid confusing menus 12%, Other 1%. The top bar (61%) is pale mint green #A7E6CB and the other five bars are blue #00689D; bars are horizontal with the value printed just right of each bar end in bold black. No legend. Right chart: title 'Primary Setting for Voice Usage, USA, 2016 (superscript 2)'; categories Home, Car, On the go, Work from top to bottom; value axis 0% to 50% in 10% steps with light grey gridlines; labelled values: Home 43%, Car 36%, On the go 19%, Work 3%. Home, Car and On the go bars are pale mint green #A7E6CB; Work bar is blue #00689D. No legend and no highlighted points beyond bar colour. Both charts have a thin grey vertical baseline at zero. Footer logo: the @KPCB wordmark in green, not a photograph.

**Design**

Background white. Title band is dark teal #00517A with a thin bright teal rule #00B2CA beneath it. Title text is white #FFFFFF in Arial regular (sans-serif), about 4.4% of slide height per line, left aligned. Chart headings and all data labels, category labels and axis tick labels are Arial bold in black #000000; chart headings about 3.0% of slide height, data and axis labels about 2.0 to 2.6%. Body and footnote text is Arial regular in black #000000 at about 0.9%; running head and page number are Arial regular in grey #A6AAA9 at about 1.5%. Accent colours: mint #A7E6CB and blue #00689D for bars. Flat shapes with square corners, no shadows, no gradients, no borders on bars.

**Layout**

Full-width header band across the top with the two-line white title left-aligned at about 2% margin. Below it, two columns separated by a vertical light grey rule at about 53% of width: the left column holds four stacked rows (1 Pre-1980s to 1990s-2010s), the right column holds three rows (Today = Complex Computing, Today = Smart / Connected Cars, Tomorrow = Computers Go Mobile?) plus a caption under the final image. Each row is a centred text block beside its picture, separated by thin horizontal grey rules. Source note bottom-left beside the KPCB logo, footer text and page number bottom-right.

**Visuals**

Left column, row 1: a black-and-white line drawing of an early open-top automobile with a driver at a steering wheel, drawn in fine pen lines on white, boxed, no overlay. Left row 2: a photograph-style render of a white sedan in side view against a dark blue gradient background, with a wiring harness drawn in yellow-orange through the body and labelled with the word VDM or similar small logo near the trunk; boxed, no crop. Left row 3: a screenshot of a Diagnostics Gauge Display software window with a black background, showing circular gauges labelled MPH and RPM, small gauges for INTAKE, FUEL TRIM and other readings, and a red and green colour scheme, boxed. Left row 4: a 3D rendering of a highway with several grey and white cars in lanes, a green highlighted lane arrow, and a speedometer overlay at lower right; boxed. OnStar logo: circular blue badge with white wordmark 'OnStar' and a small registered mark. Garmin GPS unit: a black handheld screen showing a map route with the label 250 and Dr. Hedgewar Marg, and the time 17:30. Right row 1: a transparent-grey 3D wireframe render of a modern car showing colourful wiring harnesses in blue, yellow, green and red throughout the body; boxed, light grey background. Right row 2: a photograph of a car dashboard with three round air vents across the top, a central touchscreen showing CarPlay icons in coloured squares, and a finger touching the screen; warm tan leather and dark carbon-look trim; boxed. Caption image: a studio photograph of a small black and white autonomous pod vehicle with teal wheels, transparent glass roof and a mesh panel, on a light grey background; boxed, not cropped. Logo at bottom left: green '@KPCB' wordmark.

**Design**

Background white #FFFFFF. Header band fill #00517A (deep teal blue) with a thin cyan rule about #1BB5C4 along its bottom edge. Title text white #FFFFFF, regular sans-serif (Arial/Helvetica), about 4.4% of slide height. Row headings bold black #000000 Arial-style sans-serif, underlined, about 2.0% of slide height. Body text regular black #000000 Arial-style sans-serif, about 1.8% of slide height, centred. Divider rules light grey #D9D9D9, 1 px. Footer text grey #A6AAA9 Arial, about 1.5% of height. Source text black Arial about 0.9% of height. Pictures square-cornered with no shadow.

Source: National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, “Policy on Automated Vehicle Deployment” (5/2013), Tesla, General Motors, Google, media reports

**Layout**

Full-width dark blue title band across the top with a two-line left-aligned white title, a centred bold chart heading below it, and a five-column grid of chevrons and green header cells with a three-row matrix down the left side labelled by vertical blue bars. The footer holds a small KPCB logo at bottom left, a left-aligned source line, and a right-aligned grey footer with page number 139 at bottom right.

**Visuals**

A matrix diagram of NHTSA automated driving system classifications with five columns L0 to L4, drawn as blue chevron arrows (#00689D) with white bold labels, followed by green header cells (#33B780) with white bold names, then rows labelled Description, Example and Time Frame on blue vertical bars. Row content: Description: L0 driver in complete and sole control of primary vehicle controls (brake, steering, throttle, motive power) at all times, warning systems do not imply automation; L1 automation of one or more primary vehicle control functions, no combination of systems working in unison; L2 automation of at least two primary vehicle control systems working in unison; L3 driver able to cede full control of all safety-critical functions under certain conditions, driver expected to be available for occasional control with sufficiently comfortable transition time; L4 vehicle can perform all safety-critical driving and monitoring functions during an entire trip. Example: L0 N/A; L1 ABS, Cruise Control, Electronic Stability Control, Park Assist; L2 Tesla Autopilot, GM Super Cruise (2017); L3 Google Car (manned prototype); L4 Google Car. Time Frame: L0 since cars invented (1760s); L1 1990s – Today; L2 2010s; L3 2010s; L4 ?. Two thin black horizontal rules separate the rows. The KPCB logo is a green wordmark at bottom left. No photographs or charts.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. Clean corporate design. Title band is dark teal-blue #00517A with a thin bright cyan rule beneath it (about #1BB5C9). Title text is white regular sans-serif (Arial-like) at about 4.3% of slide height, body text black (#000000) regular Arial-like sans-serif at about 1.8% of slide height, chart heading bold Arial-like black at about 3.0%. Chevron labels and row labels are white bold Arial-like at about 2.6%. Green header cells #33B780 with white bold Arial-like text at about 2.2%. Blue accent #00689D for chevrons and row label bars. Footer text light grey #A6AAA9 at about 1.5%. Shapes are square-cornered with no shadows or gradients.

**Layout**

Two equal columns below a full-width dark teal title band across the top; the title is left-aligned in white at the top-left of the band with a thin lighter teal rule beneath it. Each column has a centred bold column heading, then a photograph, then a screenshot-style text callout with red outline boxes. A small KPCB logo sits bottom-left with a source line beside it, and the footer text with page number sits bottom-right, all on a white field with margins of about 2 to 4 percent.

**Visuals**

Four photographs or screenshots and one logo. (1) Left column: photograph of a white two-door Google self-driving prototype car on a grey-brown asphalt road, driving left to right with a yellow-white lane line running diagonally across the lower right; behind it a flat green grass field, bare trees, utility poles and a pale blue sky with thin clouds; daylight, soft natural lighting, dominant colours white, green, brown and pale blue; the image is a full rectangle with no crop or overlay, boxed by its edges. (2) Right column: aerial-style map image titled FLEET LEARNING in widely spaced white capitals at top; dark grey-black road map with glowing yellow route traces forming a large X crossing and curved loop at left; labels 780M miles with DRIVEN ON HARDWARE-EQUIPPED CARS at left, ~100M miles with DRIVEN WITH AUTOPILOT ACTIVE* at right, and *SINCE SOFTWARE 7.0 INTRODUCTION at bottom centre; dominant colours dark charcoal, yellow and white; full rectangle, no rounded corners. (3) Left, below the photo: screenshot of Google Self-Driving Car Project web text in light grey sans-serif; a red rectangular outline (about #C00000, approx 0.4 percent stroke) surrounds the phrase We've self-driven more than 1.5 million miles. (4) Right, below the Tesla image: screenshot of serif text Tesla customers have driven 100 million miles with Autopilot active in near-black; red outline boxes (about #C00000) surround 100 million on the first line and miles with Autopilot on the second line. (5) Bottom-left: @KPCB logo in bright green (#2BB673-ish) with a bold condensed wordmark, the @ symbol in outline.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF with a dark teal header band #00517A across the top 12.5 percent. White background with a dark teal title band (#00517A) and a thin cyan-teal rule beneath it (about #00A3C4). Title text is white in a regular grotesque sans-serif (Arial-like), about 4.4 percent of slide height per line. Column headings are black bold Arial (Helvetica-like), about 3.0 percent of slide height. Footer text is light grey (#A6AAA9) Arial at about 1.5 percent of slide height. Source line is black Arial at about 0.9 percent. Red callout outlines are #C00000 with square corners and no shadow. Photographs have square corners and no shadows. No gradients.

KPCB INTERNET TRENDS 2016 | PAGE
143

**Layout**

Four equal columns separated by thin vertical light-grey rules, under a full-width title bar at the top; each column has a bold centred three-line heading (underlined third line) followed by a centred stack of italic captions and photos. Source line and @KPCB logo sit in a footer band at the bottom left, with the running head and page number at bottom right; margins are about 2 percent on the left and right.

**Visuals**

Photographs and logos, no charts. Column 1: 1768 Cugnot steam tractor photo (sepia-toned interior, brick-arched windows behind, boxed, rectangular, no crop shown); 1876 Otto four-stroke engine engraving (black-and-white line illustration on white); 1886 Benz Patent-Motorwagen black-and-white photo (three-wheeled car, outdoor, bare trees behind, boxed); 1888 Flocken electric car colour photo (dark brown carriage with white roof, in a glass-walled museum hall with light falling in from the windows). Column 2: 1910s Model T black-and-white photo (white background, car in three-quarter view, boxed by white margin); Ford assembly line black-and-white photo (workers beside a partly built car); 1920s-1930s American Tourist Camp black-and-white photo (archway sign reading American Tourist Camp, small cabins, trees, low contrast); Eisenhower Interstate System sign (blue rounded square with four white stars and white capitals, centred); 1941 black Cadillac-style sedan colour photo (three-quarter front view on green lawn, trees behind). Column 3: Unsafe at Any Speed book cover (red background with large white and yellow capitals, cropped rectangle); Ralph Nader black-and-white portrait (man in suit at microphone on red background); Jimmy Carter colour photo (man in cardigan seated in a room, cropped rectangle); Sorry... NO GAS TODAY sign (orange-red sign with white and black lettering, rectangle); Japanese auto takeover photo (a dark car on a red-carpeted stage in front of a banner, lit by stage lights, red and dark tones); Toyota Prius silver car colour photo (three-quarter view, in front of a building, boxed); logo set: Hyundai (silver-grey emblem with HYUNDAI wordmark), Kia (red oval with KIA wordmark), SAIC (blue and white SAIC logo with Chinese characters and SAIC MOTOR text below), DaimlerChrysler wordmark (blue capitals). Column 4: DARPA Challenge photo (dusty desert landscape with city skyline in haze and a dark off-road vehicle in the foreground, full colour, boxed, no crop); logo row Ford (blue oval with white script), GM (white letters on blue square), Tesla (red wordmark), Google (multicolour wordmark), Apple (grey apple logo), Uber (black square icon with white U-shape wordmark UBER), DiDi (orange icon with DiDi wordmark and More than a journey tagline). Plus signs (+) in bold italic separate the logo groups. @KPCB green wordmark logo in footer.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. White slide body under a dark teal title bar (#00517A) with a thin cyan rule (about #19B5C5) along its bottom edge. Title in regular Arial-like sans-serif, white (#FFFFFF), two lines at about 4.4 percent of slide height. Column headings in bold Arial, black (#000000), about 2.0 percent; underlined third line. Captions in italic Arial, black, about 1.7 percent; years in bold italic. Footer source text in Arial regular black about 0.9 percent; footer running head and page number in grey #A6AAA9 about 1.5 percent. Vertical column dividers in light grey (#D9D9D9), about 1 px. No shadows, gradients or rounded corners except the rounded tile of the Eisenhower sign.

### Slide 149

**Text**

...USA =
Potential to be Global Hub of Auto Industry Again?
USA Could Benefit from Creating Space in the Automotive
Regulatory Framework to Foster Innovation
1) Federally Provided Guidance to States to Embrace Autonomy – Multiple legislative
frameworks from individual states could impede autonomous innovation...
2) Flexibility of Regulation – Numerous approaches to solving autonomy challenge are likely to
evolve simultaneously... regulation should not impede any single innovation approach...
3) Individual Cities / States Championing Autonomy – More testing locations / forward-leaning
cities like Mountain View, CA / Austin, TX / Kirkland, WA / Metro Phoenix, AZ...
4) Comprehensive Safety Frameworks – Gov’t should have power to allow autonomous systems
that demonstrate quantifiable safety improvements over current driver-vehicle combination...
5) Leaning Forward on Sharing (Car & Ride) – Regulators should work with rather than against
sharing companies to craft policy as consumer demand illustrates need / interest in sharing...
6) Auto Cybersecurity – Connected cars face increased risk of cyber attacks...manufacturers &
suppliers should keep consumer security / privacy as a key priority...
7) Next-Generation Franchise Laws – Semi-autonomous & autonomous cars are likely to change
process of buying / servicing given ‘over the air’ nature of software downloads...USA could
consider the EU ‘Block Exemption’ as model & allow consumers to service vehicles at either
manufacturer-affiliated or independent locations
Source: KPCB Green Investing Team, Reilly Brennan (Stanford), Google
Note: EU Block Exemption details per European Commission. Testing locations represent Google autonomous car testing cities.

Behind the car another man in a dark coat and cap sits on the vehicle, a faint older automobile is at far left, and a woman in a long orange dress and wide-brimmed hat stands at right. The background is hatched buildings in cream and orange with ochre highlights. Boxed, rectangular, not cropped, with no overlay. Dominant colours: cream #F5E6C8, black #1A1A1A, red #D9322B, orange #E8733A. The bus is viewed from the side at a slight angle, centred in the frame. Boxed, with slightly rounded or irregular corners as scanned, no overlay. Dominant colours: greys ranging from #111111 to #E0E0E0. ### Slide 151

**Text**

Global Perspective on Auto Industry Future – By Region, per / Morgan Stanley Auto & Shared Mobility Research / N. America – Some home field advantage on tech innovation & early application of shared / mobility, but culture of private ownership and litigious USA judicial system may slow progress. / China – Government focus on technology / environment, as well as quality of ride-sharing / companies (esp. Didi), have driven strong early sharing adoption. Competing investment in / public transit and impact of car ownership on social standing may impede full-scale adoption. / India – Offers all key ingredients (rapid urbanization, limited public infrastructure, large / millennial population, internet inflection point) for shared mobility leadership. Current market / structure is likely to change as shared mobility gains dominance, so future remains unclear. / Europe – Lack of homegrown tech champions coupled with power of OEMs (particularly / Germans) and quality of European public transit may make adoption more difficult. High fuel / costs and strong emissions standards may drive movement forward. / Japan – Social implications of an aging population and policy support (given importance of a / strong automotive industry) represent key advantages, but OEM buy-in to new paradigm is / crucial, and R&D investment in tech arena lags somewhat behind other geographies. / Korea – Strong technological culture, early political support and sharing-focused younger / demographic leaves Korea relatively well positioned for move to shared mobility, though / adoption remains in its infancy. / Source: ‘Global Investment Implication of Auto 2.0,’ Morgan Stanley Research, 4/19/16, led by Adam Jonas / KPCB INTERNET TRENDS 2016 | PAGE / 150

### Slide 154

**Text**

Car Ownership Costs (Money + Time) = High
Car Ownership Costs = High
$8,558 / Year, USA = Depreciation @ 44% / Fuel @ 15% / Finance + Fees @ 14% /
Insurance @ 14% / Maintenance + Repair @ 9%
Commuting Time = Significant
4.3 Hours per Week per Worker, Average (13% of Work Week, USA)
Urban Auto Commuting Delays = Rising
42 Hours / Year / Urban Worker, USA (+2x in 30 Years), Equivalent to ~1.2 Extra Work Weeks / Year
Millennials = Driving Differently
Drivers License Usage Declining (Age 16-44) = @ 77% vs. 92% (1982, USA)
Millennial Willingness to Car Share = @ ~50% (Asia-Pacific) / @ ~20% (North America)
46% of Millennials Expect Vehicle Technology to do Everything a Smartphone Can...
KPCB INTERNET TRENDS 2016 | PAGE
153

biking. Average USA work week per OECD Employment Outlook (7/15). Urban auto commuting delays per Texas A&M Transportation Institute / INRIX 2015 Mobility Scorecard (8/15); delays defined as
extra time spent during the year traveling at congested rather than free-flow speeds by private vehicle drivers / passengers for 471 US urban areas. Driver's license rates per University of Michigan
Transportation Research Institute / Federal Highway Administration (1/16). Car sharing statistics per Goldman Sachs Research (5/15). Millennial expectations per AutoTrader 2016 Cartech Impact Study
(9/15, n=1,012).

### Slide 168

**Text**

China Mobile Internet Usage Leaders... / Tencent + Alibaba + Baidu = 71% of Mobile Time Spent / Share of Mobile Time Spent, April 2016 / Daily Mobile Time Spent = ~200 Minutes per User, Average / Tencent / WeChat / QQ / QQ Browser / Tencent Video / Tencent News / Tencent Games / QQ Music / JD.com / QQ Reading / All Others 29% / WeChat 35% / QQ 10% / Alibaba / UCWeb Browser / Taobao / Weibo / YouKu Video / Momo / Shuqi Novel / AliPay / AutoNavi / Baidu / Mobile Baidu / iQiyi / PPS Video / Baidu Browser / Baidu Tieba / 91 Desktop / Baidu Maps / All Other / Note: Grouping of apps include strategic investments made by Tencent, Alibaba and Baidu. Only apps in top 50 by time spent share are called out. Source: QuestMobile, Trustdata, and / Hillhouse estimates. / @KPCB / Hillhouse Capital / PAGE / 167

**Layout**

A full-width dark teal title band runs across the top 12.5 percent of the slide with a two-line left-aligned white title starting at about 2 percent from the left edge. Below it, the pie chart with a centred two-line bold chart title sits in the left and centre area, and three stacked boxed legend groups with coloured group labels occupy a right-hand column from about 63 to 96.5 percent of the width. A footer row at the bottom carries the KPCB logo at left, a small note and source line, the red Hillhouse Capital square logo with its bold wordmark, and the page number at far right.

**Visuals**

Chart: pie chart titled Share of Mobile Time Spent, April 2016 with subtitle Daily Mobile Time Spent = ~200 Minutes per User, Average. The pie has many slices; only three are labelled on the slide: WeChat 35 percent (largest slice, green gradient, upper right of centre), QQ 10 percent (blue-grey gradient slice below WeChat), and All Others 29 percent (large pale blue-grey slice covering the left half). Unlabelled slices in the lower left and bottom are small and carry no printed values. Highlighted groups: a dark red #C00000 outline wraps the WeChat slice together with the QQ slice and the small slices at the bottom; a light green outline (#A7E6CB) wraps slices at lower left; a cyan outline (#00B5CC) wraps the upper left slices next to All Others. Legend: three boxed lists. Tencent box (red outline) lists WeChat, QQ, QQ Browser, Tencent Video, Tencent News, Tencent Games, QQ Music, JD.com, QQ Reading. Alibaba box (light green outline) lists UCWeb Browser, Taobao, Weibo, YouKu Video, Momo, Shuqi Novel, AliPay, AutoNavi. Baidu box (cyan outline) lists Mobile Baidu, iQiyi / PPS Video, Baidu Browser, Baidu Tieba, 91 Desktop, Baidu Maps, All Other. Each legend entry has a small colour swatch matching its slice colour. Logos: @KPCB wordmark in green at bottom left; Hillhouse Capital red square logo with white HILLHOUSE CAPITAL text at bottom right. No photographs or icons.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. White background with a full-width dark teal header band (#00517A) and a thin cyan rule (#02B5CC) beneath it. Title text is white regular Arial/Helvetica sans-serif, about 4.4 percent of slide height per line, left aligned. Chart title and labels are bold black Arial, about 3.0 percent for the chart title and 2.6 percent for slice labels. Legend text is regular black Arial, about 2.2 percent of slide height. Group labels are bold Arial at 3.3 percent: Tencent in #C00000, Alibaba in #A7E6CB, Baidu in #02B5CC. Pie slices use vertical gradients: WeChat from pale green #A7E6CB at top to deep green #1E8C55 at bottom; QQ from blue-grey #A9B8D8 to dark blue #2E5C94; All Others from pale blue #D2E0F7 to grey-blue #A9B8D0. Legend boxes have square corners with stroke widths of about 3 px in their group colours. Footer text is grey #A6AAA9 for the KPCB line and black for the note. No shadows.
