**Layout**

Two side-by-side line charts fill the body in two equal columns beneath a full-width blue title band; the title sits top-left, left-aligned, in two lines. Each chart has a bold centred two-line heading above it, a y-axis title rotated vertically at its left, and a bottom row of year labels. The footer runs along the bottom: KPCB logo at left, source note in small type, then a red Hillhouse Capital logo block, wordmark and grey 'PAGE 171' at right. Margins are about 2 percent on the left and right.

**Visuals**

Two line charts. Left chart: title 'Share of China Total Retail Revenue*, 2010 – 2015'; y-axis '% of China Retail Sales', range 0% to 7% in 1% steps with gridlines; x-axis years 2010 to 2015. Series Alibaba (blue line): about 0.4% in 2010, about 1.1% in 2011, about 1.9% in 2012, about 2.9% in 2013, about 4.6% in 2014, about 6.5% in 2015 (ends highest point at top right). Series JD.com (green line): starts 2013 at about 0.9%, about 1.7% in 2014, about 2.8% in 2015. Legend inside plot area at upper left: Alibaba blue line, JD.com green line. Right chart: title 'Share of USA Total Retail Revenue*, 2010 – 2015'; y-axis '% of USA Retail Sales', range 0% to 7% in 1% steps; x-axis years 2010 to 2015. Series Amazon.com (blue line): about 0.8% in 2010, about 1.2% in 2011, about 1.7% in 2012, about 2.1% in 2013, about 2.6% in 2014, about 2.9% in 2015. Series eBay (green line): about 0.5% in 2010, about 0.5% in 2011, about 0.6% in 2012, about 0.8% in 2013, about 0.9% in 2014, about 0.9% in 2015. Legend inside plot area at upper left: Amazon.com blue line, eBay green line. No highlighted points. Lines are about 3 pt thick with no markers; gridlines are light grey. KPCB logo: small green wordmark '@KPCB' at lower left. Hillhouse Capital logo: red square with white 'HILLHOUSE CAPITAL' text and a white vertical line, not cropped.

**Layout**

Two-column content slide under a full-width dark teal header band. The left column holds a vertical bar chart with its title above it, the right column holds a donut chart with its title above it, and both sit in the middle band of the slide. The title is left-aligned in the header with a small left margin of about 2% of slide width. The source line sits bottom-left beside the @KPCB logo, and the Hillhouse Capital logo block with the page number sits bottom-right.

**Visuals**

Left: vertical bar chart titled '% of WeChat Users Making E-Commerce Purchase Through WeChat'. Y-axis titled '% of Surveyed WeChat Users', range 0% to 40% with gridlines at 10% steps. X-axis categories 2015 and 2016. Single series, bars in #00689D: 2015 = 15% (value labelled above bar), 2016 = 31% (value labelled above bar). No legend. Bars are about 2.5% of slide width each, centred on their category positions. Right: donut chart titled 'Channels Through Which Users Made E-Commerce Purchase', white centre hole, segments clockwise from top: JD Mall featured within WeChat 32% in green #31AF78 (about 32% of ring), WeChat Public Accounts 23% in blue #00689D, Group Chats or Friends Circle 23% in cyan #02B5CC, Links to Other Apps 22% in crimson #C82055. Each segment label is white bold text placed inside its segment, with the percentage on its own line below the name. No legend, no highlighted points, slight drop shadow under the ring. Bottom-left: @KPCB logo in green #31AF78 pixel-style wordmark. Bottom-right: Hillhouse Capital logo, a red #E31B23 square with small white 'HILLHOUSE CAPITAL' lettering and a short white vertical line below it, set on a white rectangle.

**Design**

Background: Solid white #FFFFFF. White content background with a dark teal header band (#00517A) across the top about 12.5% of slide height, with a thin bright cyan rule (#02B5CC) along its bottom edge. Title text is white in an Arial-style regular sans-serif, roughly 4.4% of slide height per line. Chart titles and axis labels are black Arial Bold (sans-serif) at about 3% of slide height for chart titles and about 2.2% for axis labels and values. Body and source text are Arial regular, grey #A6AAA9 for the page footer and black #000000 for the source line at about 0.9% of slide height. Bar chart bars are flat #00689D with no outline. Gridlines are thin light grey. Donut segments are flat fills with no outlines and a soft shadow on the ring edge.

**Visuals**

Two charts. (1) Left: line chart titled Outbound Departures as % of Population, 1970 – 2015. Y axis titled Outbound Departure as % of Population, linear, 0% to 35% in 5% steps, gridlines light grey. X axis years 1970 to 2015 labelled every three years (1970, 1973 ... 2015), labels rotated vertical. Series: China (red #C00000, line starting about 1996 near 0.4% and rising to about 8.8% by 2015; values are not printed, estimates only), Japan (blue #0A5E9E, starting 1971 near 1% and rising to about 13% to 14% from 2005 onward, peak about 14.5% around 2012; values about), S. A pale yellow band #FFD961 at 50% opacity spans the plot from about 5% to 10% highlighting that range. **Layout**

A full-width dark blue title band runs across the top 12.5% of the slide with a thin teal rule beneath it; the title is left-aligned in two lines inside the band with a margin of about 2.1% from the left edge. Below, two charts sit side by side in the upper half (Marketplaces at left, Commerce at right, each with a bold centred heading and a two-line subtitle), and a third chart (Enterprise) is centred in the lower half. The KPCB logo sits bottom left, the source notes run in four small lines along the bottom from x 10.5%, and the running footer 'KPCB INTERNET TRENDS 2016 | PAGE 185' sits bottom right with the page number on a second line beneath. There is no slide number other than the printed 185 in the footer.

**Visuals**

Three line charts, all time shifted and with no printed data values. (1) Marketplaces chart: title 'Marketplaces'; subtitle 'Gross Merchandise Value (GMV), Time Shifted / Alibaba vs. eBay vs. Airbnb vs. Uber'. Y axis 'GMV ($B)', range $0 to $20, gridlines every $5 at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20. X axis 'Years Since Launch (T+)', ticks 1 to 8. Series, all estimated: Alibaba / Taobao (yellow) about $0.1 at T5, $0.3 at T6, $1.3 at T7, $2.7 at T8. eBay (pale mint) about $2.8 at T5, $5.4 at T6, $9.3 at T7, $14.8 at T8. Legend box with four entries, each a thick line swatch in its series colour followed by its label, stacked vertically at upper left of plot. Logos placed at line ends: eBay wordmark above the eBay line end; UBER wordmark above the Uber end; airbnb wordmark right of the Airbnb/eBay area; Alibaba Group logo at the Alibaba end. (2) Commerce chart: title 'Commerce'; subtitle 'Gross Merchandise Value (GMV), Time Shifted / Amazon.com vs. JD.com'. Y axis 'GMV ($B)', range $0 to $200, gridlines at 0, 50, 100, 150, 200. X axis 'Years Since Launch (T+)', ticks 1 to 20. Series: JD.com (red-orange) about $0.5 at T7, $5 at T8, $10 at T9, $19 at T10, $39 at T11, $71 at T12, line ends at T12. (3) Enterprise chart: title 'Enterprise'; subtitle 'Est. Quarterly Revenue ($MM), Time Shifted / Salesforce vs. Slack'. Y axis 'Revenue ($MM)' with no tick labels, five horizontal light grey gridlines and no values. X axis ticks 1 to 13 (no axis title). Series: Salesforce (purple) rises from the baseline at T1 to about the top gridline at T13, passing about T5 low, T8 mid-low, T13 highest; ends at T13. Slack (teal) starts with Salesforce at T1 and rises steeply to about one-third height at T5, ending at T5. Legend box at upper left with Salesforce (purple) and Slack (teal) line swatches. **Layout**

Full-width header band across the top 12.5% of the slide holds a two-line left-aligned title with about 2% left margin. Footnotes, source lines, the KPCB logo at lower left and the footer with page number 191 at lower right sit in the bottom band.

**Visuals**

Chart: combined vertical stacked bar chart with a line overlay, titled Global US-Listed Technology IPO Issuance and Global Technology Venture Capital Financing, 1990 – 2016YTD. Y-axis is labelled Annual Technology IPO and Technology Private Financing Volume ($B), range $0 to $200 with gridlines at $50, $100, $150 and $200. X-axis is years 1990 to 2016 plus YTD, rotated about 45 degrees. Each bar stacks a dark-to-light blue Technology Private Financing Volume ($B) segment at the bottom under a green Technology IPO Volume ($B) segment. Printed total labels per year, in order 1990 to YTD: $3, $3, $8, $7, $5, $14, $26, $19, $28, $89, $157, $58, $28, $22, $36, $40, $36, $42, $34, $25, $33, $48, $50, $44, $107, $96, $48. The 2000 bar is clipped at the top of the plot and its label reads $157. Line series: NASDAQ, cyan line drawn continuously from about 1990 at about $38 equivalent to about 2016 at about $185 equivalent with peaks near 2000 and 2015; no printed values on the line except the two callouts. Highlighted points: callout March 10, 2000 = NASDAQ @ 5,049 with an arrow pointing to the 2000 peak of the line; callout July 20, 2015 = Technology Market Peak, NASDAQ @ 5,219 with an arrow pointing to the 2015 peak. Legend at upper left of plot: green swatch Technology IPO Volume ($B), blue gradient swatch Technology Private Financing Volume ($B), cyan line NASDAQ. ### Slide 198

**Text**

Data = A New Growth Platform...
Powering New Services / Systems / Apps
Sources of Leverage for Global Internet Growth
The
Network
Large investments in fiber optic & last-mile cables created connectivity that facilitated the early Internet growth
The
Software
Optimizing the network with software became far more capital efficient than additional capex buildouts...ultimately resulting in the creation of pervasive networks (siloed data centers → AWS)...& then pervasive software (Siebel → Salesforce)
The
Infrastructure
Emergence of pervasive software created the need to optimize the performance of the network & store extraordinary amounts of data at extremely low prices
The
Data
Next Big Wave = Leveraging this unlimited connectivity & storage to collect / aggregate / correlate / interpret all of this data to improve people’s lives & enable enterprises to operate more efficiently
Source: Adam Ghetti, Ionic Security; Ted Schlein, KPCB.
KPCB INTERNET TRENDS 2016 | PAGE
197

**Layout**

Four horizontal rows stacked top to bottom inside a wide content area, each row a blue label tile at left followed by a bordered text box at right. A vertical gradient arrow runs down the left margin with its rotated label beside it. The title sits top-left in a full-width dark blue header bar; the source line is bottom-left beside the @KPCB logo, and the footer with page number 197 sits bottom-right. Left margin about 2 percent, right edge of the row boxes about 95 percent.

**Visuals**

Vertical downward block arrow at the left, about 7.4 percent wide and 77 percent tall (x 1.8, y 15.7), with a light grey to mid grey vertical gradient (top about #F2F2F2, bottom about #A0A0A0) and a thin #00689D outline; its label reads Sources of Leverage for Global Internet Growth in bold blue #00689D, rotated to read bottom to top. Four rows, each with a rounded blue tile (#00689D) holding a bold white label and a white rectangle with a #00689D outline holding black body text: The Network (fiber optic and last-mile cables, early Internet growth); The Software (optimizing the network with software, pervasive networks in italics from siloed data centers to AWS, then pervasive software in italics from Siebel to Salesforce, arrows drawn as right arrows); The Infrastructure (pervasive software, optimizing network performance and storing data at low prices); The Data (Next Big Wave, leveraging connectivity and storage to collect, aggregate, correlate and interpret data, with the phrase improve people’s lives & enable enterprises to operate more efficiently underlined). Logo @KPCB in green at bottom-left. No photographs, charts or tables.

**Layout**

Three-column layout on a white field under a full-width dark blue title band: column headers FIRST WAVE, SECOND WAVE and THIRD WAVE sit centred above each column, with a bold statement and three centred lines of body text beneath. Title is left-aligned in the band at top left; a footer carries the @KPCB logo and source line at bottom left and the KPCB INTERNET TRENDS 2016 | PAGE 198 running footer at bottom right, with no slide number element other than the printed 198.

**Visuals**

Diagram of stacked rounded-rectangle boxes in three columns with horizontal rows labelled Software (green), Security (light blue) and Infrastructure (crimson) down the left side. First column: BI box (Business Objects, Cognos, MicroStrategy), Data Integration box (Informatica), Data Integrity box (Microsoft, Oracle), and Age of Oracle, Sybase box. Second column: five stacked small green boxes VISUALIZATION, CLOUD BI, CACHING, PREP / WRANGLING, ETL; then Infrastructure-centric Security & Management box (Palo Alto Networks, FireEye) and Age of Big Data box (Hadoop, Teradata, Netezza, NetApp, EMC, Greenplum). Third column: Departmental Applications (Gainsight, Datadog, InsideSales), Organization-wide Analytics Platforms (Looker, Domo, Anaplan), Data-centric Security & Management (Ionic Security, Tanium), Age of Big/Fast (Redshift, BigQuery, Spark, Presto). Two large white chevron-type block arrows with grey outlines point rightward between the columns: the first labelled Evolution / Breaking Apart Data Bottleneck, the second labelled Revolution / Data Integrated into Everything. No charts, photographs or photos.

### Slide 208

**Text**

Data Privacy Debate – Major Events, 2013 – 2016
Edward Snowden
(Jun-13)
Former CIA contractor leaked classified information to media
about internet & phone surveillance by USA intelligence.
Burr-Feinstein Anti-Encryption Bill
(Apr-16)
Proposed law that would require technology companies & phone
manufacturers to decrypt customer data at a court’s request.
Apple vs. FBI
(Feb-16)
FBI claimed it needed Apple to provide access to an iPhone
owned by a man who committed a mass shooting in San
Bernardino, CA, so that the agency could recover information
for its investigation. Request was denied by a federal judge in
New York.
.
Microsoft Lawsuit
(Apr 16)
Files lawsuit for right to be able to tell customers when law
enforcement officials request their emails & other data.
WhatsApp’s Default End-to-End Encryption
(Apr-16)
WhatsApp implements end-to-end encryption as default
setting to protect communications of their 1B monthly active
users worldwide.
Apple Hires Data Security Expert
(May-16)
Jon Callas, who co-founded several well-respected secure
communications companies including PGP Corp, Silent Circle and
Blackphone, rejoins Apple (he was also an employee in the 1990s
and again between 2009 and 2011, when he designed an encryption
system to protect data stored on a Macintosh computer).
Source: NY Times, CNBC, Reuters, Time, Washington Post, WhatsApp.

207
